pageCache.pageTitle: Henry Fawcett Primary School - PE and Sports Premium
pageCache.text:
PE and Sports Premium
PE and Sports Premium helps us to train our staff and teach our children through a bespoke sports programme. Our Sports Coach teaches children different sports during lunchtime and playtime. Pupils have been taught a wide variety of sports including athletics, tennis, cricket, football and rounders. Our Sports Coach also provides daily after school sports clubs and provides sports activities in our wrap around care.
Our Sports Coach has allocated time to support children with specific physical or behaviour needs; allowing these children to access the full sports curriculum. Children with special educational needs are provided with support according to their needs.
We aim to ensure gifted and talented children are given challenges to develop their skills further.
We identify pupils who have particular sporting skills and school sports teams are participating in competitions, sporting events and tournaments.
We have developed a school wide plan for improved and enhanced P.E. provision. We have appointed a dedicated P.E. coordinator to ensure a continued delivery of a wide range of sporting opportunities and increased involvement with sports groups and organisations in the community. P.E. and Sports Funding has meant that all pupils have an increased awareness of the importance of keeping healthy and which activities can help them lead a healthy, happy life.

pageCache.pageTitle: Henry Fawcett Primary School - How to apply for Reception Class
pageCache.text:
How to apply for Reception Class
If your child was born between 1 September 2022 and 31 August 2023, you must apply for a primary or infant school place for September 2026.
You must apply for a Reception place at Lambeth Council Primary School Admissions. Children who attend the Nursery do not transfer automatically to the main school. You should make your application within the specified dates for that academic year.
Apply on time and apply online! The deadline for applications is midnight on 15 January 2027. Henry Fawcett will contact successful applicants by the end of May.
Important Information
It is important to know how the primary school application process works and what you need to do and when.
Please read the Lambeth starting primary school booklet for full information about the admissions process and criteria for each Lambeth state school: Starting primary school in Lambeth 2027-28 booklet
You may also find it useful to read the summary guide: A brief guide to starting primary school in Lambeth 2027-28

pageCache.pageTitle: Henry Fawcett Primary School - After School Clubs
pageCache.text:
After School Clubs
We are delighted to offer a range of FREE after school clubs again this term! Ensuring equal access for all pupils is deeply important to us, and our team works hard to secure external funding to make this possible. This term, clubs are provided free thanks to Qualiteach Education, Football567 and Hyde Housing.
To give everyone a chance across the year, club groups will refresh each term (Autumn, Spring, and Summer). (Note: Clubs for Nursery and Reception children will begin in Spring 2027). Sign-up will be by Parent Mail.
Autumn Term Schedule
All on-site clubs run directly after school until 4:30 PM and prompt collection is important.
Wednesday
- Football (Mixed) (with Dan): Develop fundamental ball skills, game understanding, and team play.
Thursday
- Farm Club (Year 3-6) (at Vauxhall City Farm): Games and hands-on animal handling. Runs 1st October to 22nd October. Collection is at 5:00 PM directly from Vauxhall City Farm.
- Art & Craft (with Betty): Get creative with fun arts and crafts projects.
- Music Club (with Dan): Use technology and instruments to compose and record original music.
- Multisports (with Sofiane): Try out a variety of energetic sports and active group games.
Friday
- Girls United Football (Girls Only) (with Coach Francisco): Focus on building football skills, confidence, and teamwork in a dedicated environment.

pageCache.pageTitle: Henry Fawcett Primary School - Our Vision & Values
pageCache.text:
Our Vision & Values
Our vision
At Henry Fawcett, our mission is to build a school community where every child, every family and every member of staff can say:
I belong. I matter. I am great at learning. I am not afraid of challenges. I am living my best life. I am ready for the future.
Our vision is rooted in strong relationships, high expectations and a deep belief in every child’s potential. We are a proud family, connected to our community, committed to ambitious learning and united by the belief that every child deserves a bright future.
Our values
Our values guide everything we do – from the way we teach and support children, to the way we work with families and each other. They shape our culture, our communication and our daily practice.
Pride – A Proud Family
We are proud of who we are and proud of our community. Children feel a strong sense of belonging and know that they matter. Families choose Henry Fawcett because of our warm, inclusive ethos and our commitment to every child’s success. Staff work with passion, integrity and teamwork to bring our vision to life. Pride is something we build together – through kindness, respect and shared responsibility.
Connection – Every Child Seen, Heard and Understood
Relationships sit at the heart of Henry Fawcett. We value our community’s diversity, talents and experiences. Every child feels seen, listened to and understood. Parents are treated with compassion and respect. Staff are trusted, supported and encouraged to grow. We believe connection comes from open communication, empathy and strong partnerships with families.
Growth – High Expectations for Every Child
We believe every child can achieve excellence – academically, creatively and personally. Our curriculum inspires curiosity, confidence and a love of learning. Children develop the skills, attitudes and motivation to do their best. Families are empowered to support learning at home. Staff development is meaningful and valued, helping us deliver ambitious teaching every day.
Resilience – Embracing Challenge Together
We teach children that progress comes from effort, reflection and perseverance. Mistakes are part of learning, and challenges help us grow. Staff model resilience through flexible, reflective practice. We work in partnership with families to strengthen resilience at home and at school. Together, we embrace new opportunities and support one another to do better.
Wellbeing – Happy, Safe and Ready to Learn
Children’s happiness and wellbeing are central to our work. We create a nurturing environment where pupils feel safe, secure and able to express themselves. Staff wellbeing is championed meaningfully, and families trust us to care for their children. We teach children how to look after their mental and physical health, and we behave in ways that help others feel safe and supported.
Empowerment – Preparing Children for a Bright Future
We want every child to leave Henry Fawcett believing they deserve success – and knowing they are equipped to achieve it. We work with local organisations to champion long‑term opportunities for our community. Families feel confident that the school is preparing their children for the future. Staff are committed to the school’s vision and understand how to make it real. Empowerment means believing in ourselves and supporting others to do the same.
Our Commitment
Henry Fawcett is a warm, ambitious and inclusive school where every child is known, valued and supported to thrive. Our Vision & Values shape our culture, our communication and our daily practice – and they guide us as we prepare children for a bright, confident and successful future.

Packed Lunch
Henry Fawcett Primary school is dedicated to providing an environment that promotes healthy eating and enables pupils to make informed food choices. This will be achieved by the whole school approach to food provision and food education documented in the School Food Policy.
Packed Lunch Guidance for Parents and Staff
Packed lunches should aim to include:
Packed lunches should not include:
Some starchy foods such as bread (sliced bread, pitta bread, wraps, bagels), pasta, potatoes, couscous; choose wholegrain where possible
1 portion of fruit and 1 portion of vegetables or salad
Dairy food such as cheese or yoghurt
Meat, fish, or another source of protein such as eggs, beans and pulses, hummus, falafel
Oily fish once every 3 weeks e.g. sardines or salmon
Crisps or crisp type snacks e.g. cheddars
Any items containing chocolate including bars, biscuits, cakes or high sugar yoghurts/desserts
Fruit juices, smoothies, squash or fizzy drinks
Food containing nuts
School Food Policy (including Packed Lunches)

Uniform and Clothing Guidance
At Henry Fawcett Primary, we see children as whole human beings and this includes how they dress. What a child wears should never be a barrier to their learning, their belonging, or feeling part of our school community.
For some families, school uniforms are one way of creating a sense of belonging and making mornings simpler. Many children enjoy wearing it as part of our shared identity, and we’re happy for families to continue doing so. At the same time, we know that clothing is also a way for children to express who they are. Feeling comfortable, confident, and fully themselves matters too.
We also understand that some children have sensory needs, and the feel or fit of certain clothes can affect their comfort and ability to focus. We encourage families to choose clothing that supports their child’s wellbeing.
We welcome all children whether they wear uniform or other clothing and support families in making choices that work best for them and their child.
Suggested Clothing for School
White or blue polo shirt
PE Days
Dark shorts or tracksuit bottoms
Trainers
Outerwear
We spend time outside every day, in all weathers, so children will need a warm coat on cold days, and a waterproof jacket in rainy weather. In summer, we encourage sun hats.
Accessories and Expression
Children are encouraged to express their cultural heritage, gender identity and individuality through their clothing, hair, and accessories. We only ask that clothing and accessories are safe for active play and learning. If you have any concerns or queries we are happy to discuss.
With this in mind, jewellery is limited to small stud earrings and watches only. Other types of jewellery should not be worn to school.
Keeping clothing safe
We ask parents to write their child's name inside all clothing so that we can reunite lost clothing with their owners.
As a school that values children’s right to play and explore, we understand clothing may get messy or worn during active learning. We ask parents to take this into account when choosing school clothes.

pageCache.pageTitle: Henry Fawcett Primary School - About Us
pageCache.text:
About Us
About Us - Welcome to Henry Fawcett Primary School
Henry Fawcett is a warm, ambitious and inclusive school at the heart of our community. We are a proud family where every child is known, valued and supported to thrive. Our vision is rooted in strong relationships, high expectations and a deep belief in every child’s potential.
We want children to feel happy, safe and ready to learn every day. That means creating a nurturing environment where pupils feel seen, listened to and understood – and where they are encouraged to embrace challenge, celebrate their strengths and grow with confidence.
Our curriculum is designed to inspire curiosity, creativity and a love of learning. We teach with ambition and purpose, helping children talk confidently about their ideas, make meaningful progress and take pride in their achievements. We celebrate excellence in all its forms, from academic success to creativity, leadership, resilience and kindness.
Inclusion is a whole‑school strength at Henry Fawcett. We meet children where they are and help them grow, working in partnership with families to understand each child’s needs. Our inclusive practice benefits every child – not just those with SEND - and reflects our commitment to wellbeing, equity and opportunity.
We are deeply connected to our local community. Our partnerships enrich learning, broaden horizons and help children see themselves as capable, confident contributors to the world around them. Whether through creative arts, sports, local projects or leadership opportunities, pupils learn that their voices matter and that they can make a positive difference.
Henry Fawcett is a place of pride, connection and growth. A place where children feel they belong. A place where they are empowered to build a bright future.
We are delighted to welcome you to our school.

Admissions
We encourage you to visit our wonderful school and see our fantastic learning environment. Our school is an exciting and vibrant place where every pupil has a wide range of opportunities and learning experiences.
We welcome all visits to the school whether your child is starting nursery, reception or mid-year. All tours are with the Headteacher.
To reserve a date to visit Henry Fawcett Primary School, please contact the school office on 0207 735 2764 or email admin@henryfawcett.lambeth.sch.uk
If your child is approaching the age of 3 years old you can apply for a part-time or full-time place for them in our Nursery. You should apply directly to the school when your child reaches the age of 2 years old. An application form must be completed and you should draw attention to any special reasons to support the application, for example if your child has medical needs. Parents can apply for their statutory free 15 hours of childcare and a 30 hour free place if eligible.
For the 30 hours free childcare, applicaitons should be made via the Direct Gov website: https://www.gov.uk/apply-30-hours-free-childcare
